Q1: The failure was seen only on PR #7044's head `ai/issue-6769` at commit c659fa81b380. That PR is still open and unmerged into `main`, so the PR's own changes are the likeliest cause. Building the fix on that branch, with an `Integration branch: ai/issue-6769` line, puts it where the failure is. If #7044 merges first, the merged-base retarget (`RETARGET_MERGED_BASE_ENABLED`, on by default) moves the fix PR's base on its own.
Q2: The CI step already prints each shard's full log in its own group (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1629-1631`). The test name exists in the run log; the triage just didn't capture it. So no `ci.yml` change is needed, and option B would add scope that needs the automation-path grant. The implementer has no network access and can't fetch the run log. Re-running the same partition locally is the reliable way to find the failing test. Running group 3, shard 0 means:
- build the remaining-tests list the way `ci.yml` does, minus the fast-fail subset;
- take `NR % 4 == 3` of that list for the group, then `NR % CI_POLL_TEST_SHARDS(4) == 0` for the shard.

If that slice doesn't reproduce the failure, run the whole `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` module. Then make the smallest fix for the first real failure:
- If a test and the code disagree, decide which side is wrong from the documented behaviour (agents.md, README, changelog fragments, the issue behind #6769). Don't rewrite the test just to match the current code.
- If nothing fails, record it as a flaky or environmental failure and make no code change.
